EventItemActionText:
Present: Mr. Condon, Mr. Petersen, Mr. Creed, Mr. Gadell, Mr. Rettinger, and Mr. Lowther.
Absent: Mr. Dhanjal.
Staff Present: Zoning Administrator, Andrea West, and Board Clerk, Patricia Taylor

BZA-26151 — 203 Albea Court NE
Request for approval of a variance from the required front yard setback in the RS-12.5 Zoning District for the construction of a foyer and entryway addition that encroaches into the front yard setback. 
Ms. Andrea West, Zoning Administrator, was sworn in and presented the staff report. She explained that the property is a split-level home located on a cul-de-sac with a sloped front yard. The applicant proposes a foyer and covered entry addition, a portion of which would encroach up to approximately one foot and eight inches into the required 30-foot front yard setback. She noted that covered porches are permitted to encroach; however, enclosed living space requires Board approval through a variance.
Ms. West described the lot configuration, including the curvature of the cul-de-sac and slope of the property, and reviewed submitted plans and photographs.
There were no Board questions. 
The applicant, Ms. Marie Armstrong, was sworn in and presented the request. She stated the addition is intended to improve functionality of the home, including providing adequate entry space and weather protection. She noted that due to the slope of the lot and configuration of the cul-de-sac, expansion to the rear or sides is constrained. She stated that expansion into the back yard would require building into the hill and disturbing a lot of land and the lot is too narrow for side expansion. She mentions that it is hard to open the door of the home and enter due to the door being so close to the stairs, which is the only point of entry. The applicant stated that neighboring property owners had been notified and were generally supportive of adding on the front. 
Mr. Tad Davidovich, representing Hinsdale Design Build, was sworn in and provided additional testimony. He stated that alternative design options were considered, including expansion to the rear; however, drainage and grading issues made that approach impractical. He confirmed that the proposed encroachment is minimal and varies slightly along the frontage due to the curvature of the lot. He also stated that the building restriction line follows the curvature of the cul-de-sac. 
There were no board questions.
Board members discussed the hardship criteria, including the unique lot shape, slope, and cul-de-sac configuration. Members noted that the encroachment is minimal and that the proposal is consistent with the character of the neighborhood for a variance approval.
No public comments were received.
Mr. Creed made a motion to close the public hearing. Mr. Gadell seconded the motion. The motion carried.
Motion: Mr. Peterson moved to approve the variance request for the front yard setback at 203 Albea Court NE, as presented.
Second: Mr. Condon
The hardship was explained by Mr. Peterson. He mentions the house was designed at an angle to face the cul-de-sac. The angle of the dwelling follows the arc of the sidewalk and cul-de-sac, which is at an extreme arc. This meets the requirements for hardship.
Vote: With a roll call vote, the motion carried 6–0.

The Board reviewed the previous meeting minutes. Mr. Creed noted that future minutes should include more detailed summaries of questions and responses to ensure a complete record. 
Motion: Mr. Petersen moved to approve the meeting minutes as submitted.
Second: Mr. Rettinger. 
Vote: The motion carried unanimously.

Mr. Condon moved to adjourn the meeting.
Second: Mr. Gadell
The motion carried unanimously.
The meeting adjourned at 7:57 p.m.

About the Board of Zoning Appeals

About the Board of Zoning Appeals:

The Board of Zoning Appeals is a quasi-judicial board comprised of seven members – all of whom are residents of the Town of Vienna. The Board serves as an arm of the Fairfax County Circuit Court, as all members are appointed to the Board by the Court after receipt of a recommendation from the Vienna Mayor and Town Council.  

 

The Board of Zoning Appeals is empowered by the Code of Virginia, as defined in Section 15.2-2309, to: 

Grant variances from the Zoning and Subdivision Ordinance in accordance with Section 18-843 of the Town Code.  

Grant Conditional Use Permits in accordance with the provisions of Section 18-824 of the Vienna Town Code. 

Decide appeals from any order, requirement, decision, or determination of the Zoning Administrator.  

Decide applications for interpretation of the Zoning District Map when there is any uncertainty as to the location of the boundary line.  

 

The Board decides each application on its own merit – there are no precedents. The Board of Zoning Appeals hears only sworn testimony, with each meeting participant sworn in before offering remarks. After hearing testimony and discussion, the Board will vote on each agenda item before moving to the next. The granting of an appeal, Conditional Use Permit, or variance requires an affirmative vote of a quorum, no less than a majority of the membership (4), of the Board. If any party is not satisfied with the decision of the Board, an appeal may be filed with the Circuit Court of Fairfax County within 30 days of the decision.
